benefits: 105 high school juniors will each receive up to $25,000 to support their pursuit of the American Dream through higher education
Scholarship funds may be applied to any line-item in your Cost of Attendance
Funds will be sent directly to your college to be credited to your account

Scholars join a community committed to supporting them academically, personally and professionally, beginning with the 12-month College Success Program (individualized coaching, workshops and online resources through the senior year of high school)
Scholar services include academic planning, college selection advising, financial aid counseling, emergency and housing support, mentoring, and internship stipends
eligibility: Be enrolled full time as a high school junior in the United States

Exhibit a strong commitment to pursue and complete a bachelor's degree at an accredited non-profit public or private institution in the United States immediately after high school graduation (students may start their studies at a two-year institution and then transfer to a four-year institution)
Demonstrate financial need ($100,000 or lower adjusted gross family income is required)
Be involved in co-curricular and community service activities
Display integrity and perseverance in overcoming adversity
Maintain a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 2.0
Be a United States citizen (U.S. permanent residents, green card holders and DREAM Act recipients do not qualify)
requirements: Complete the online application during the published application period; one application enters you for consideration for all scholarships you are eligible for, except some Specialized Scholarships
Write essay responses describing your Horatio Alger story and sharing your American Dream experience
Provide a high school transcript that includes fall grades
Provide income verification, most often the parents' tax form; an IRS tax transcript is an alternative, and government benefit statements where no return was filed
Provide your school counselor's email so the counselor can submit the Counselor Certification Form
Provide the email of an adult over the age of 21 who is not related to you and is familiar with the adversity described, to serve as Support Form Provider and confirm the adversity section
Verify U.S. citizenship when accepting the award
documents: High school transcript (must include fall grades)
Income verification: parents' tax form, IRS tax transcript, or statement copies of government benefits for non-filers
Counselor Certification Form, completed online by the school counselor
Support Form Provider confirmation of the adversity section, completed online
Proof of citizenship uploaded when accepting the award: passport photo page, birth certificate, citizenship certificate, or Consular Report of Birth Abroad
selection_criteria: Resilience in overcoming significant personal challenges
coverage: Scholarship funds may be applied to any line-item in your Cost of Attendance
Funds will be sent directly to your college to be credited to your account
Up to $25,000 in higher education funding, requested online each May for the upcoming year of study
application_method: Click the Apply Now button during the application period to start the online application

official.description: The National Scholarship annually awards 105 high school juniors up to $25,000 each in higher education funding. While most other scholarships focus exclusively on academic achievement or leadership potential, Horatio Alger Scholarships are also intended for promising students who have critical financial need, demonstrate integrity and perseverance in overcoming adversity, and are determined to succeed.
official.region: United States - all 50 states and Washington, D.C.
official.program_type: Need-based scholarship from the Horatio Alger Association of Distinguished Americans, Inc., a 501(c)(3) educational nonprofit; National Scholarship for high school juniors

applicant_utility.summary: The National Scholarship pays up to $25,000, sent straight to your college against any Cost of Attendance line item, but only to current high school juniors - the December 1 to March 1 window falls during 11th grade, so seniors who wait a year cannot use this award. Test scores do not matter (there is no SAT/ACT minimum and the only GPA floor is 2.0), which means the essays on overcoming adversity, plus online confirmations from your counselor and an unrelated adult over 21, carry the application. Since one application also enters you for the Association's other scholarships, the effort can pay off more than once. Line up the transcript with fall grades and a parental tax return or IRS transcript in early December, because paperwork, not the essay, is what usually holds files up.
applicant_utility.best_fit: U.S.-citizen high school juniors from households under $100,000 adjusted gross income with a 2.0+ GPA, community involvement, and a specific, well-documented story of overcoming adversity.
application_readiness_checklist: Open the application in the first week of December - the essays on your Horatio Alger story and American Dream experience are the core of the file

Warn your counselor and your chosen support provider to watch for the Association's automated emails in early December; school filters routinely block them, and after two failed resends you must contact the Association directly
Finish the adversity section completely BEFORE your Support Form Provider confirms it - the section locks once they submit and cannot be edited
Request an IRS tax transcript early if parents cannot produce a return: PDFs are immediate, mailed copies take 5-10 days, and you must write your name next to your social security number on it
Confirm your intended college is not for-profit or online - the Association will not send funds to proprietary institutions
Upload everything inside the portal - nothing is accepted by mail, email or fax, and there is no fee to apply
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 12:00 p.m. ET cutoff on March 1 - late applications are categorically not accepted
Counselor or Support Form Provider never completing their online forms, leaving the file incomplete at the deadline
Submitting income documents on the Association's not-accepted list (W-2s, 1099s, check stubs, bank statements, free/reduced lunch letters, SNAP or TANF statements, state or foreign tax returns)
Adjusted gross family income above the $100,000 ceiling
Adversity section locked mid-edit after the provider confirms, so the story the committee reads is unfinished
Planning to enroll at a for-profit or online college, which the Association does not fund
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything beyond the up-to-$25,000: the remaining Cost of Attendance (tuition balance, housing, food, books, transport) must come from federal or state aid, work-study, or family contribution. If other awards cover your full Cost of Attendance you must notify the Association so the funds can be re-awarded.
document_audit: The transcript must include fall grades - request it only after fall grades have posted
If parents do not file taxes, use statement copies of government benefits (public assistance, disability); handwritten returns and benefit worksheets are rejected
The Support Form Provider must be over 21 and unrelated - a neighbor, family friend, counselor, pastor or teacher, not a relative
Proof of citizenship (passport photo page, birth certificate, citizenship certificate or Consular Report of Birth Abroad) is only needed once you are notified, but keep it accessible
alerts: Only selected applicants are notified, by email and mail in April/May - silence is a rejection
The National Scholarship is juniors-only; the February 15 senior deadline covers the Association's senior-level programs, not this one
Funds must be requested again every May for the upcoming year, so keep full-time enrollment and a clean college account
There is no application fee and no SAT/ACT minimum - do not rule yourself out on test scores
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online between December 1 and March 1: submit essays and personal data, trigger the counselor certification and support-provider emails, upload the transcript and income documents in the portal, and complete everything by 12:00 p.m. ET on March 1; the support provider's confirmation locks the adversity section.
